obligations.note: At head, payments policy.py sets PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES = 16 and controls/payments/policy-params.json sets payments.privileged_idle_minutes = 16. The approved bound is <= 15. The passing control test only compares the code to the edited 16-minute parameter, so it doesn't show the 15-minute limit is met.

The change relies on EXC-0184. That exception is approved by a risk owner and unexpired, but it is scoped to component mortgage.session, not payments.session, so it doesn't cover this payments SES-1 deviation. The only payments SES-1 exception, EXC-0141, expired on 2026-09-08 and covers only batch service-account sessions.

Ticket CHG-26996 is a standard ticket, approved by change manager grace.kim on 2026-10-04T00:27Z, before the change opened at 21:27Z. Its components (payments.policy, payments.controls-data) cover policy.py and controls/payments/policy-params.json. The file list comes from the change description because git diff was unavailable.
sofia.santos approved the code review. She holds the change_approver role for payments and is a different person from the author, linh.nguyen.
Both approvals name the single, final commit f72ea53, so no later commits exist to void them.

The CI run on f72ea53 succeeded with 172 tests, 0 failures and 0 skipped, including the registered SES-1 control test test_privileged_idle_timeout_within_policy. As a process record this is complete, but that test compares against the edited parameter, so it doesn't establish SES-1.

The change edits the protected file controls/payments/policy-params.json. rachel.stein (control_owner, controls-office, outside the author's payments-eng team) approved head commit f72ea53. Approving the change process doesn't cure the substantive SES-1 violation.
The change is marked non-emergency and ticket CHG-26996 is type standard, so no post-implementation review is required.

No acceptance-ledger entry covers the payments session or idle-timeout code. The PAY-1 and AUD-2 entries in policy.py's scope cover symbols whose values (10000.00 and 7) are unchanged, so no evidence lapses.

summary: The change raises payments' privileged-session idle timeout to 16 minutes in both code and controls data, which violates SES-1's approved bound of 15 minutes. The exception it relies on, EXC-0184, is scoped to the mortgage.session component, not payments.session, so under EXC-1 it can't excuse the deviation. CI passes only because the SES-1 control test checks the code against the edited parameter value. The process records (ticket, independent review, control-owner approval, CI on the final commit) are otherwise in order, but a refuted product obligation requires rejection. CHG-5 is left out: the described files (policy.py, policy-params.json) aren't marked security-sensitive, though git access was blocked so I couldn't confirm the full changed-file list.
